chunks: And Saad ibn Abdullah narrated, from a group of our companions, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'There is an occultation for the Young Man (the Imam) before he rises (to claim authority).' I asked: 'Why?' He replied: 'He fears.' And he pointed with his hand to his belly. Then he said: 'O Zurarah! He is the Awaited One, and he is the one in whose birth people doubt. Some of them say: When his father died, he had no heir; some say: He was a fetus; some say: He is hidden; some say: He has not yet been born; and some say: He was born two years before his father's death. And he is the Awaited One, but Allah the Exalted loves to test the Shia, so at that time the false ones will waver in doubt.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, if I live to see that time, what should I do?' He said: 'O Zurarah, if you live to see that time, then supplicate with this supplication: O Allah, make me know Yourself, for if You do not make me know Yourself, I will not know Your Prophet... until the end.'

key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: The Young Man (a title for the Twelfth Imam)
key_terms.الْمُبْطِلُونَ: The false ones / those who deny the truth
key_terms.جَعَلْتُكَ فَدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of deep reverence)

ai.seo_question: What are the reasons for the Imam's occultation and the doubts regarding his birth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological concept of 'ghaybah qabl al-qiyam' (occultation prior to rising), emphasizing that the Imam’s concealment serves as a divine trial (*ibtilah*) to distinguish true believers from the doubtful. The detailed enumeration of conflicting public opinions regarding the Imam’s status—whether he is a fetus, a child, or already born—underscores the era of *al-istidraj* where uncertainty prevails, making spiritual vigilance and specific supplications crucial for theologically for the Shia community.
